criteria.no: The account only assures compliance, lists the topic, states a conflicting policy, or contains no compliance support.
criteria.unclear: A possible supporting artifact appears but its relationship to the preference is indeterminate.
criteria.yes: A specific source path/diff, named test or output, executed command, or concrete source/cost comparison supports the preference.

evidenced.instructions: Does the account in `item.text` give checkable support for its claim of implemented conditional cheaper-REST preference? Judge evidence supporting the claim, not the existence of generic artifacts.

criteria.no: No delivered conditional preference is stated, or the description explicitly abandons it.
criteria.unclear: The topic is present but the account does not establish the delivered preference.
criteria.yes: The delivered REST preference under the cheaper-and-sufficient condition is explicit. An equal-cost or insufficient-REST exception may accompany it.

implemented.instructions: Read `item.text` as an account of completed work. Does it state that equivalent required stack information is obtained preferentially through REST when that costs less quota than GraphQL? A comparison may be stated as a policy; no numeric measurement is necessary for this judgment.

criteria.no: The work only changes an unrelated subject.
criteria.unclear: The work description is too vague to establish the subject.
criteria.yes: The change selects, acquires, or depends on remote stack information.

relevant.instructions: Is the subject of the delivered change in `item.text` within `anchor.scope`: selecting REST or GraphQL to obtain remote stack information?

criteria.no: No such conflicting choice is stated. Equal cost and incomplete REST are outside the condition.
criteria.unclear: A described choice could bypass cheaper sufficient REST, but facts are ambiguous.
criteria.yes: A stated delivered choice bypasses sufficient cheaper REST in favor of GraphQL.

violated.instructions: Is a delivered decision in `item.text` incompatible with preferring REST when sufficient required information costs less than GraphQL? Judge only stated conflict: absence of the preference is not a violation.

anchor.scope: Selects REST or GraphQL for remotely acquiring stack information.
anchor.statement: The sc-gh-stack redesign must prefer REST to GraphQL when REST supplies the required information at lower quota cost.

item.text: Changed sc-gh-stack remote information acquisition code and shipped the new implementation. The account gives no details of REST, GraphQL, or cost-based source selection.
